public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 277

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/277](https://www.erdosproblems.com/277)
- [Ha79] Haight, J. A., Covering systems of congruences, a negative result. Mathematika (1979),
  53--61.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos277

/--
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos277.lean#L1294"]
theorem erdos_277 :
   answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧
      ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i  := by
  sorry

end Erdos277

reformulations.difference: The theorem encodes moduli as ideals of ℤ and expresses nonexistence of a covering by universally quantifying over StrictCoveringSystem ℤ and requiring some modulus ideal not to contain n. It also quantifies n over ℕ without explicitly requiring positivity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonzero proper ideal of ℤ is uniquely dℤ for a natural d>1. Its translates are precisely residue classes modulo d, and distinct ideals correspond to distinct positive moduli. Membership n∈dℤ means d∣n, so ∀ covering systems, ∃ a modulus not containing n is exactly the negation of existence of a covering whose moduli all divide n. Furthermore, σ(0)=0 makes the strict inequality impossible at n=0. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, source_statement_iff proves the full equivalence with a positive-n statement using the divisor sum and finite coverings by distinct natural moduli greater than 1, without using the theorem under review.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's question and affirmative answer. The source currently records PROVED (LEAN), agreeing with all status metadata. Boundary checks included σ on 0–12, n=1 for c<1, impossibility of an empty covering index, and an explicit strict covering with moduli 2,3,4,6,12. Both the equivalence proof and the cited external proof compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Haight's full text was inaccessible; its covering-system definition was checked in the publisher's extract. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
